Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Ireland's reply. The umpires are out in the middle. Bangladesh players are seen in a huddle, near the fence. Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie will open up for Ireland. Ebadot Hossain has the new ball in hand. Let's go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

With a massive 509 to chase, the focus shifts entirely to the Irish batters. Can they show the necessary grit and determination to bat for survival and force a draw? The task is monumental, and given the current run of play, it looks incredibly difficult. They will need a performance for the ages to deny Bangladesh a dominant victory. Stay tuned for Ireland's reply in a short while...

The partnership continued to frustrate the Irish attack, with Mominul Haque playing a stellar innings. Eventually, Mominul fell for a superb 87, which was the signal for the captain to call the batters in. Bangladesh declared their second innings on 297/4, setting a mammoth, and arguably impossible, target of 509 runs for Ireland. The Irish bowlers struggled throughout, with Andy McBrine, Jordan Neill, and the two-wicket taker Gavin Hoey unable to significantly halt the flow of runs.

Bangladesh finally declare on 297 with a massive lead of 508 runs! Bangladesh started Day 4 with a clear goal, to push the lead past 500. Though they lost the set opener Shadman Islam and Najmul Hossain Shanto early, the experienced pair of Mushfiqur Rahim and Mominul Haque absorbed the pressure. They batted beautifully throughout the morning session, stitching a crucial partnership and ensuring the scoreboard kept ticking. By the end of the session, they had reached a commanding 280/3, extending the lead further and keeping Ireland's bowlers toiling hard for little reward.

OUT! TAKEN! Gavin Hoey strikes. That's a soft dismissal. Much fuller, outside off, Mominul Haque looks to drive it but the ball hits the upper part of his bat and carries towards Curtis Campher at cover who makes no mistake. Mominul Haque makes his way back and Mushfiqur Rahim follows him as Bangladesh declare on 297/4 with a massive lead of 508 runs!

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second session of Day 4. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Mominul Haque and Mushfiqur Rahim will resume their innings. Gavin Hoey will start with the ball. Let's go...

We will catch you after the Lunch break and see what approach Bangladesh take from here. Quick runs will surely be the aim, which looks almost a certainty, so be ready to witness plenty of strokes flying to every corner. The action will resume at 6.10 am GMT, so do not wander too far away. In the meantime, you can switch over to the Ashes or the New Zealand vs West Indies 3rd ODI to keep your cricketing appetite fed. See you soon.

For the record, Bangladesh are just 9 runs short of a 500-run lead, and one can expect them to chase that landmark rather than get caught up in individual milestones. To be honest, on this pitch and with the quality of spinners Bangladesh possess, it should not be too demanding for them to pick up 10 Irish wickets. No disrespect to Ireland, but they have lacked the skills to counter spin so far, and there is little reason to expect a dramatic change in that script.

Earlier in the day, Shadman Islam did not add much to his overnight score, but Mominul has brought up his third fifty of the series, and if Bangladesh decide to bat for another hour or so after Lunch, he will have his eyes firmly on a century that has eluded him so far. Playing his 100th Test, Rahim sits on 44, and under the same logic, he too has a golden chance to become only the second man after the great Ricky Ponting to score a century in both innings of a Test match. These are the storylines still alive in this contest, because the match itself has become completely one-sided.

Mushfiqur Rahim wraps his arms around Mominul Haque as the duo walks away to enjoy Lunch. Bangladesh continue to march along in this Test match, and make no mistake, the scoreboard is walking right alongside them. Yes, they stumbled early with two wickets falling in quick succession, but with a lead of this magnitude, pressure never really came knocking on their door. Ireland's bowling once again drifted into the mediocre category, but on the rare occasions when they hit the right areas, there was plenty of assistance waiting for them. The problem was consistency. And Bangladesh happily cashed in on every loose delivery that came their way.

Lorcan Tucker, who was the only shining light in that dismal Irish batting card, comes up for a quick chat. The young man shares that his experience of playing here as a U19 player helped him and reminds us that he had success in 2023 as well. He mentions his partnerships down the order and praises his partners, Jordan Neill and Stephen Doheny. Also adds that they kept taking confidence from each other. Calls it a tricky surface and feels it is only going to be difficult to bat on. Signs off by saying that you have to trust your skills and be positive.

Bringing our focus back to the game in hand here, we are just minutes away from the start of Day 4. After looking listless with the ball last evening, Ireland will be desperate for improvement. Their plan is simple enough on paper - keep hunting for wickets and if breakthroughs refuse to arrive, at least clamp down on the scoring rate. Bangladesh, on the flip side, will be itching for two hours of pure batting blitz. If things go their way, a target creeping towards the 500 mark could very well be part of their game plan. It is the kind of morning where one side dreams of damage control (if not already out of control), and the other dreams of damage.

Let us update you - England picked up the final wicket soon after our last update and gained a handy 40-run lead. On the other side, Temba Bavuma is again lucky with the toss and South Africa will be batting first.

What a cracking Saturday of cricket we've got - the sport has taken over the globe and fans are happily powerless! In New Zealand, the West Indies are throwing everything at the hosts in the 3rd ODI, hunting a consolation win which looks unlikely at the moment, with 7 of the West Indian wickets gone down for less than 100. The Ashes is in pure chaos mode again - 19 wickets fell on Day 1, however, 20 minutes into Day 2, England are still trying to pick the last wicket. And around 450 km away from here in Mirpur, a bruised India are facing the reigning Test champions South Africa in the 2nd Test, tension is high there as well in Guwahati.

So instead of rolling the dice with the follow-on, the hosts chose to pile on the runs at an excellent tempo, tightening Ireland into a corner. Another couple of hours of solid batting on Day 4, and the hosts will almost seal the equation to just two results - a draw, or a win for themselves. The visitors are already on the ropes, and if Bangladesh land a few more punches this morning, it could be curtains pretty quickly.

Just a reminder, Bangladesh did have the opportunity to enforce the follow-on on Day 3, despite Ireland's last five wickets showing tremendous fight and adding 171 invaluable runs. That gritty batting display made Bangladesh feel their bowlers had earned a breather, and a second hit with the bat seemed the smarter call. And of course, there was that little voice of caution, what if Ireland's batting suddenly clicks, Bangladesh might have been left chasing on a wearing surface, and that is never a happy proposition in Test cricket, especially on subcontinent pitches.

With a commanding lead of 367 runs, it's an understatement to say that Bangladesh are in complete control of the match. Their batting was outstanding, and a near-clinical bowling performance followed it in the first innings. The aggressive intent they showed with the bat last evening in the second innings was equally impressive.

Hello and a very cheerful welcome to Day 4 of this Test match in Mirpur. The sun is shining and Bangladesh will walk out today with the confidence of a team that has already picked its spot on the victory podium. Ireland, on the other hand, arrive with one clear mission - survive. The scoreboard looks a bit like a horror movie for them, and the only question now is whether they can turn this into a heroic escape story. So settle in, dear readers, if the Tigers start roaring early, this could be the final day of this Test series. But if Ireland decide to dig in and fight, the humour will be on us for thinking Test cricket ever follows logic.

However, a moment of brilliance from Taijul Islam saw two wickets fall in three balls, with the partnership between Stephen Doheny and Lorcan Tucker of 81 also broken. But a surprising performance from Jordan Neill saw another crucial partnership of 74 runs but much like Doheny, Neill fell against the run of play as the second new ball brought Bangladesh success. Now the onus is on Bangladesh to extend their lead to such a state that it almost becomes impossible for Ireland to think of climbing the mountain. On the other hand, Ireland will hope for wickets on Day 4. The first hour will be very crucial. Join us for the all-important day at 3.30 am GMT. You can join us earlier for the build up. Until then, cheers!

Earlier in the day, Ireland put up a great fight, surprisingly pushing Bangladesh hard. Lorcan Tucker's steady recovery was key, as Ireland were reeling at 98/5 at the start of the day's play.  The way Tucker and Stephen Doheny began the day was pleasing as their proactive approach cut the deficit bit by bit and put the game in a firm balance. Not just Ireland's batting but Bangladesh were a bit reckless with the ball, allowing the visitors to get back in the game.

The openers, Shadman Islam and Mahmudul Hasan Joy laid a fantastic platform, scoring 119 runs together with both batters crossing their respective fifties. Mahmudul Hasan Joy fell but Shadman Islam is going strong along with Mominul Haque at the moment. Earlier, the home team started with a significant lead of 211 runs. Bangladesh had a chance to enforce the follow-on but their bowlers were tired under the sun after fielding for 88.3 overs. It feels like it was a correct decision by Najmul Hossain Shanto as Bangladesh are all over Ireland at this point.

Well, Bangladesh were dreaming of crossing the 500 mark in the first innings, but it looks like they'll get their wish on Day 4 as they have delivered a superb performance in the final session. Jokes apart! Bangladesh lead by 367 runs at the end of day's play and are hungry for more. With 9 wickets in hand, Bangladesh have put themselves on a brilliant platform and have one foot over the victory line. Ireland had their moments but none made a significant impact. They rolled with spinners mostly. Andy McBrine was decent, Gavin Hoey tried to extract turn off the rough, but the home team were just too good, as nothing dampened their intent

... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

The opening pair of Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam have made their intentions pretty clear in how Bangladesh plan to approach this innings, showing positive intent from the outset as they look to set up a declaration. This approach will create opportunities for Ireland, and it will be crucial for them to hold on to every chance that comes their way. Jordan Neill was off with his lines and lengths, and we could well see spin from both ends after the break. Do join us at 8.30 am GMT for the final session.

With no chances coming their way and the Irish pair moving along nicely, Bangladesh took the second new ball as soon as it was available. That did the trick, as Neill was removed soon after. Tucker was happy not to farm the strike, showing trust in Gavin Hoey and Matthew Humphreys, but they couldn’t offer the resistance he needed, leaving Lorcan stranded as Ireland were bowled out for 265.

SESSION SUMMARY - 26.3 overs, 95 runs and 3 wickets. A productive period with the bat caps off a good session for Bangladesh. Despite their efforts to dig deep earlier in the day, Ireland ended up conceding a 211-run lead, and with the ball, they haven’t begun the way they would have liked, leaking runs upfront. Ireland started the session 265 runs adrift, and Lorcan Tucker and Jordan Neill picked up right where they left off before the break. Neill continued to collect boundaries square of the wicket, while Tucker remained solid as a rock in defence.
